title.narrative: Sustainable Management and Conservation of Wildlife

description.narrative:
To achieve community consultation, UNESCO with the support of the Ministry of Wildlife Conservation and Tourism and the Ministry of Culture, Museums and National Heritage will work together to mobilize and engage local communities residing in parks including local administration in the GPAA government to sensitize them on the importance of conservation and the benefits of putting their own site on the global list of World heritage property. The consultation process led by an international expert with support from a national expert will take place in the form of meetings, training sessions, focus group discussions, community radio talk shows and questionnaires. Key stakeholders during community consultation would include all 17 ethnic groups such as women, youth, men, traditional leaders, chiefs, from Murle, Jie, Anyuak, Mundari, Bari, Pari, Dinka, Nuer, Latuka, Lopit sampled by geographical locations in Jongeli, GPAA, Central and Eastern Equatoria States respectively. The aim is to raise awareness about the benefits of world heritage nomination, understand the role of these communities in conservation of BBML, and understand their need, and issues about the conservation of BBML, to be considered in the nomination processes.
It will also work with Enjojo Foundation (EF), a non-profit organization dedicated to managing protected areas in collaboration with governments and local communities through a conservation model that promotes peace, supports sustainable livelihoods and enterprises, and enables socio-economic stability. To empower local populations surrounding LNP to generate income while promoting environmental conservation by supporting beekeeping and honey production. 40 community members will be trained and equipped in sustainable beekeeping and honey production. Will also engage with White Eared Kob Heritage Society to conduct workshops against poaching of white eared kobs and preserve its spectacular annual migration phenomenon in Akobo - South of Sobat Basin migratory corridor that the white eared kobs traverse for pasture and water to the confluence of Sobat and Gilo rivers. This will not only ensure protection against poaching, but human encroachment on wildlife habitats such as human resettlement, roads construction projects and oil prospection activities. This will enable the community to benefit not limited to supports socioeconomics development through tourism initiatives maintenance of Biodiversity and ecosystems functions. Retention of symbols of cultural heritage for the people of South Sudan; build livelihoods amongst the communities to abandon hunting and focus on agriculture, entrepreneurship and other resilient means of livelihoods; facilitates protection of wildlife habitats alongside infrastructure development act as a research conduit for wildlife and cultural researchers; both locally and internationally.
